name: All One-Unit Opposite-Wing Comparisons Reduce to One Central Square
statement: Let an ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ of order at most nine, and suppose both terminal wings have two-cycle holonomy and excess at most one. Either their acquired supports contain three pairwise disjoint direction pairs, or $B$ is the unique exceptional graph consisting of a central four-cycle with a pendant path of length two at each of two antipodal vertices, and both wings have the $\eta=1$ form based at the other antipodal pair. In the exceptional case, if $z_1,z_2$ are the square directions and $f_1,f_2$ the tail directions, the four terminal supports are exactly $\{\{z_i,f_j\}:i,j\in\{1,2\}\}$.
proof: Every one-unit wing is either eta-one or extra-owner, and every zero-unit wing is sharp. Sharp--sharp is impossible, while extra-owner comparisons without an eta-one wing are incompatible or yield three disjoint supports. For an eta-one wing, both terminal supports are acquired above and absent from $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$; the same holds for the ordinary extra-owner support and sharp terminal supports. The shadow-intersection identity forbids a support acquired by both wings. The eta-one comparison theorem then eliminates the repeated-pair alternatives against sharp and extra-owner wings, and against a second eta-one wing leaves three disjoint pairs or precisely the exceptional central-square graph with the displayed complete bipartite support system.
